meta.title: Bengali Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 101 expressions · 49 everyday, 39 idioms, 13 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 101 Bengali set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 49 everyday phrases, 39 idioms and 13 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Bengali → English (see the Bengali, recall the meaning) and English → Bengali (see an English meaning, recall the Bengali) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Bengali A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the levels. The Phrases subdeck holds greetings and wishes of both communities (শুভ সন্ধ্যা, ঈদ মোবারক, শুভ বিজয়া), the phrasebook sentences a learner needs whole (আমার সাহায্য লাগবে, আমি জানতে চাই, আমার প্রশ্ন আছে) and the set everyday expressions (কিছু না, বার বার, দেখতে পাওয়া) — the first greetings and questions of all (আসসালামু আলাইকুম, শুভ সকাল, আপনি কেমন আছেন, আপনার নাম কি) are cards of Bengali A1, where a beginner needs them; the Idioms are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (ঘোড়ার ডিম, 'a horse's egg', means nothing at all); the Proverbs are complete sayings. WHERE THESE COME FROM: every expression of English Wiktionary's Bengali that no level teaches was read, and these were chosen by hand; compound nouns (bird and plant names, 'laptop computer'), second spellings, personal sentences about one's faith or nationality, partisan slogans, religious formulas in Arabic, and vulgarities were left out. The dictionary's Bengali is small, so this deck is too. Within each subdeck the expressions stand in the order a learner can read them: first those whose every word a card of Bengali A1 shows, as a headword or among its forms, then those that need A2, and so on (24 at A1, 9 at A2, 9 at B1, 7 at B2, 1 at C1, and 51 with a word no level teaches); among expressions of one level the commonest come first, by a frequency list built from film and television subtitles. The app deals the three subdecks side by side. Every expression is printed in the Bengali script with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it and, where the dictionary gives one, its pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet. Real example sentences come with 16 of the 101 expressions. At Folio's default of ten new cards a day — which is five expressions a day, each being two cards — this deck takes 21 days. Sources. Meanings and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
